entry.title: Debugging Non-Deterministic LLM Agents: Implementing Checkpoint-Based State Replay with LangGraph Time Travel
entry.summary:
Introduction
Large Language Models (LLMs) are inherently non-deterministic even with identical inputs and parameters, they generate different outputs on each execution. This fundamental characteristic creates a critical challenge for production AI systems: how do you debug, audit, and reproduce agent behavior when the execution trace disappears after each run? In this technical deep-dive, we explore LangGraph's Time Travel feature a checkpoint based state persistence system that transforms ephemeral LLM agent executions into reproducible, debuggable workflows. We demonstrate the implementation through a real-world banking use case where a loan rejection needed to be investigated, debugged, and corrected in production. entry.title: Key Components of Microsoft Fabric Explained in Simple Terms
entry.summary:
Microsoft Fabric is built as a single platform that brings different data tools together. Instead of using many separate services, Fabric connects everything into one system. To understand how Microsoft Fabric works, it is important to know its key components and the role each one plays. OneLake:
Data Factory: Data Factory is used to collect and move data from different sources. These sources can be databases, cloud storage, or business applications. Data Factory helps bring raw data into Fabric and prepare it for further processing. It supports low-code pipelines, which makes it beginner-friendly. Synapse Analytics: Synapse Analytics handles data processing and analysis. It is mainly used for cleaning, transforming, and organizing data. This component is useful for data engineering tasks and working with large datasets. It ensures data is ready for reporting and analysis. Power BI: Power BI is used for reporting and data visualization. It converts processed data into charts, dashboards, and reports. Since Power BI connects directly to OneLake, reports always reflect the latest data without extra steps. How These Components Work Together First, data is collected using Data Factory. Because all components are connected, the workflow remains smooth and easy to manage. Conclusion: Microsoft Fabric components are designed to work as one system. OneLake stores data, Data Factory moves it, Synapse processes it, and Power BI visualizes it. This integrated setup reduces complexity and makes Microsoft Fabric easy to understand, even for beginners starting their data analytics journey. “The guide is curated by FabricExperts with practical explanations.”
